, with a continuous distribution. A bigeodesic is a doubly infinite path whose finite segments are geodesics for the induced passage-time metric. Furstenberg–Kesten's bigeodesic conjecture. Almost surely, there are no bigeodesics in dimension two. This is a central question in first-passage percolation; the paper proves the absence of bigeodesics with one end in any deterministic direction under differentiability of the limit-shape boundary, but the unrestricted conjecture remains open.

OPEN · PROGRESS REPORTED

The conjecture remains open, although an unverified conditional manuscript claims to extend the known finite-moment result to all continuous edge-weight laws.

Furstenberg’s conjecture, recorded via Kesten, asserts that almost surely no bigeodesic exists for continuous i.i.d. edge weights on the two-dimensional square lattice. The unrestricted statement remains unresolved.

KNOWN RESULTS

Licea–Newman (1996) ruled out bigeodesics with prescribed asymptotic directions outside a null set.
Wehr–Woo (1998) obtained related fixed-direction nonexistence results.
Damron–Hanson and Ahlberg–Hoffman proved nonexistence for each deterministic direction where the limit-shape boundary is differentiable, under finite-mean assumptions.
Later work constructed direction-specific geodesic graphs without doubly infinite paths, but explicitly did not settle simultaneous absence in all directions.

OCTOBER 2026 CONDITIONAL EXTENSION

A submitted manuscript argues that the stipulated finite-moment no-bigeodesics theorem extends to every nonatomic edge-weight law, removing the moment assumption and claiming absence of all bigeodesics. This is conditional on the upstream theorem and its proof inputs, and remains unverified; it is not independent validation of the unrestricted conjecture.

Current status (as of October 2026): the unrestricted two-dimensional conjecture remains open; fixed-direction results under limit-shape differentiability are established, while the new all-directions extension is an unverified conditional claim.
